      Wyndham Championship Best Bets and Golf Odds

      Wes Reynolds previews this week's PGA Tour stop, the Wyndham Championship in Greensboro, N.C.

      By
      Wes Reynolds
      -
      August 4, 2026
      289193
      X
      Facebook
      Email

        Wyndham Championship Best Bets and Golf Odds:

        Listen to audio version of this article
        Sponsored by
        0:00 / 19:46
        Instaread

        Former U.S. Junior Amateur (2018) champion Michael Thorbjornsen was promoted to the PGA Tour two years ago for finishing atop the PGA Tour University rankings from his time at Stanford. He got his first tour victory on Sunday at the Rocket Classic courtesy of a 30 on the back nine to shoot 63 for a winning score of -18 to win the event by two strokes at a pre-tournament price of 45-1. 

        Xander Schauffele finished two back at -16 for outright second. Davis Riley (-15) was the 54-hole leader but settled for solo third after carding three bogeys in his first six holes and letting the field back into the tournament. Rasmus Højgaard finished fourth at -14, and a four-way tie rounded out the top 5 at -13 with Hideki Matsuyama, Matt Wallace and Kris Ventura.

        Thorbjornsen was at No. 69 in the FedExCup points and now does not have to concern himself with making the playoffs as he vaulted to No. 38.

        This week is the final event in the chase to get into the FedExCup Playoffs as the PGA Tour heads to Greensboro, N.C., for the Wyndham Championship. 

        Cameron Young (+850), who played his college golf at nearby Wake Forest, won his long-awaited first PGA Tour event last year here. 

        Like Thorbjornsen, Jackson Koivun (20-1) earned his tour card through PGA Tour University, but he got his first victory in just his third tour start at the 3M Open two weeks ago.

        Matsuyama (25-1) comes into this week with consecutive top-5 finishes in both the 3M Open and Rocket Classic. 

        Ben Griffin (28-1) finished fourth here at the Wyndham in 2022 and seventh in 2024.

        Ryan Gerard (30-1) was our nearest contender last week, finishing T-8. 

        At 33-1 are Justin Thomas and reigning PGA Champion Aaron Rai, who won at the Wyndham two years ago. 

        Scottish Open winner Tom Kim (36-1) won his first PGA Tour event four years ago here at the Wyndham. 

        Other former Wyndham champions in the field this week include 2023 winner Lucas Glover (150-1), 2019 winner J.T. Poston (66-1), 2007 and 2018 winner Brandt Snedeker (250-1), 2014 winner Camilo Villegas (600-1) and 2011 winner Webb Simpson (250-1), a North Carolinian who also played at nearby Wake Forest and named one of his daughters Wyndham in honor of the event that was the site of his first PGA Tour victory. 

        The Event

        The Wyndham Championship was established in 1938 as the Greater Greensboro Open (Wyndham Hotels & Resorts took over as sponsor in 2007). The event has a lengthy history and has been the site for several PGA Tour records. In 1965, Sam Snead set PGA Tour records for being the oldest player to win a PGA Tour event (age 52) and for most wins at a sole event (eighth win). Fifty years later, in 2015, Davis Love III won here at age 51 and became the oldest player to win on the PGA Tour in the Senior/Champions Tour era (1980).

        The Field 

        147 players are in this week’s Wyndham Championship field playing for an $8.5 million purse, with $1.53 million going to the winner. 

        However, most of these players are playing for FedExCup points. The following players are on the bubble to make it into the FedExCup Playoffs. Here are the scenarios for each of these players:

        The following players must win this week to qualify for the playoffs: Max McGreevy, Beau Hossler, Adrien Dumont de Chassart, Jesper Svensson, Matthieu Pavon, Chris Kirk, Karl Vilips, Haotong Li, Gordon Sargent, Brice Garnett, Chad Ramey, Pontus Nyholm, Hayden Springer, Jimmy Stanger, Ben Silverman, Hank Lebioda, Davis Chatfield, Ben James, Matt Kuchar, Takumi Kanaya, David Skinns, Patrick Fishburn, Erik van Rooyen, Luke Clanton, Aaron Wise, Joe Highsmith, Kevin Streelman, Paul Peterson, Lanto Griffin, Trace Crowe, Adam Schenk, Ben Martin, Danny Walker, Dylan Wu, Brian Campbell, Jeffrey Kang, Garrick Higgo, Patton Kizzire, Nick Dunlap, Thorbjørn Olesen, Kensei Hirata, John VanDerLaan, Vince Whaley, Peter Malnati, Will Gordon, Tyler Duncan, Justin Lower, Rafael Campos, Adam Svensson, Chan Kim, Adrien Saddier, Webb Simpson and Danny Willett.

        The stakes are high for advancing in the FedExCup Playoffs — but the first step is simply getting in.

        The top 50 after the FedEx St. Jude Championship will also qualify for all Signature Events in 2027, and the top 30 after the BMW Championship will additionally qualify for the 2027 Masters, U.S. Open and Open Championship.

        Those who finish Nos. 71-100 in the standings will have full PGA Tour status for 2027, while players Nos. 101-125 will retain conditional status, although the top 100 and top 125 will not be finalized until after the FedExCup Fall concludes with The RSM Classic in November.

        The Course

        Sedgefield Country Club, in Greensboro, N.C., took over hosting the Wyndham Championship in 2008. The Wyndham is held at the Ross Course, named for its designer Donald Ross, which opened in 1926. After renovations conducted in 2007 by Kris Spence, a golf course architect based in Greensboro, who worked as the course superintendent at nearby Forest Oaks Country Club, which hosted the Wyndham from 1977-2007. 

        Sedgefield is a par-70 of 7,131 yards. It is a typical Carolina course with tree-lined fairways, pine straw and Champion Bermudagrass throughout. The course is a par-70 with only two par-5s and four par-3s. Nine of the 12 par-4s are less than 450 yards. 

        The fairways are narrow (29-yard average — 9th narrowest on tour) and the rough measures at 2.5 inches. There are five water hazards in play on six holes, and the layout is not all that heavily bunkered (52 on course — seventh fewest on tour); however, the fairway bunkers at Sedgefield are tough to reach the greens in regulation. The Champion Bermuda greens (avg 6,000 square feet) undulate and are fast (12.5 stimpmeter).

        This is a scoreable course. Brandt Snedeker shot 59 here for the course record on his way to victory at the 2018 Wyndham. 

        Here is the official scorecard for the 2026 Wyndham Championship courtesy of PGATOUR.com:

        McConnell Golf LLC owns 16 golf and country clubs throughout the Southeast, including Sedgefield. Their site provides an aerial view of the course.

        Correlated courses to Sedgefield include Waialae, TPC River Highlands, and Colonial (shorter par-70s), Detroit GC (Ross design), Harbour Town, Sea Island (Seaside course), TPC Sawgrass and East Lake (Ross design). 

        Weather

        The AccuWeather forecast shows a humid week in Greensboro with very light winds and chances of small thunderstorms in the late afternoon all four days.

        2024: Aaron Rai (-18/262); 35-1

        2023: Lucas Glover (-20/260); 90-1

        2022: Tom Kim (-20/260); 35-1

        Wyndham Championship Recent Trends

        • Each of the last five Wyndham Championship winners had at least one top-5 finish within five starts leading into the event.

        Selections

        Hideki Matsuyama (+2350, DraftKings)

        Matsuyama finished T-5 last week in Detroit but led the field for Strokes Gained: Tee-To-Green and was second for Strokes Gained: Approach. 

        Last week’s result followed up a T-3 the week prior in Minneapolis. 

        Even with the no-cut provisions in Signature Events, Matsuyama has gone 19-for-19 in making the weekend this season and has made 34 in a row dating to May 2025. 

        The driver has been what has held him back a bit this season, but he has gained strokes off the tee in each of his last four, and Sedgefield is not a place that provides much trouble off the tee. 

        Ryan Gerard (29-1, DraftKings)

        Gerard was one of the selections last week and will be so once again off a T-8 in Detroit. 

        At No. 16 in the FedExCup standings, Gerard is likely to play all three FedExCup Playoff events, but his goal is to get the victory that has eluded him in the 2026 season and make the Presidents Cup team later this fall. 

        He has three runner-up finishes this season, including the Sony Open (Waialae historically a strong correlation to Sedgefield), The American Express and the Memorial Tournament. 

        This week is also the closest event to a home game for Gerard, who grew up in Raleigh and played his college golf in Chapel Hill at the University of North Carolina. 

        Tom Kim (36-1, DraftKings)

        Kim broke a near three-year winless streak last month with a victory at the Genesis Scottish Open last month. 

        This week, he returns to the site of his first career tour victory (August 2022) at the Wyndham Championship and Sedgefield has produced a couple of winners (Davis Love III, Brandt Snedeker) who have won the Wyndham multiple times. 

        His iron play has stood out, as he ranks fifth in Strokes Gained: Approach, while he’s also fifth in Proximity from 125-150 yards, where most of the approaches will come from this week. 

        The putting has shown an uptick of late, with three of his best putting performances coming in his last six events. 

        Davis Thompson (55-1, DraftKings)

        Thompson comes into this week at the Wyndham on the back of two top-10 finishes in a row at the 3M Open and Rocket Classic. 

        He has gotten progressively better at the Wyndham over the last three years, finishing 22nd in 2023, 12th in 2024 and 11th in 2025.

        Two years ago, he finished runner-up at Detroit GC, so he has shown well at Donald Ross designs. 

        The former John Deere Classic winner is a good fit here. 

        Ben Kohles (60-1, BetRivers)

        We had some heartbreak with Kohles a few weeks back at the John Deere Classic when he looked like the clear winner but hit his approach into the water at 18 to end up finishing third. Undaunted, we are back for more.

        Kohles, a winner earlier this summer on the Korn Ferry Tour, is likely to get his PGA Tour card via that route but is also 95th in FedExCup points and the top 100 gain full tour status as well.

        He has been up and down from the Korn Ferry to PGA Tour on several occasions and is likely to be back again next year, but he has some unfinished business to get that first victory on the big tour and the Wyndham is a perfect site for him to do it, considering he made his first PGA Tour start right here at Sedgefield in 2012. 

        Ryo Hisatsune (60-1, DraftKings)

        Hisatsune finished third on debut at the Wyndham in 2024. 

        He has not missed a cut since the season opener in Hawaii, so the form has been consistent throughout the season. 

        The man from Japan arrives off a T-50 last week in Detroit but was second in the field for Greens In Regulation but struggled on the greens, so he might relish the switch to Bermuda here. 

        Blades Brown (66-1, Bet Rivers)

        Brown, 19, bypassed college to turn professional and is playing on the Korn Ferry Tour, where he is 9th on the KFT points list (the top 20 at season’s end get PGA Tour cards), but could skip that like he did college with a victory here.

        Three years ago, at age 16, Brown became the youngest medalist in stroke play at the U.S. Amateur, breaking the record of the legendary Bobby Jones.

        Brown has four top-6 finishes on the KFT plus a third at the Puerto Rico Open earlier this spring. 

        With the recent victories of Jackson Koivun and Michael Thorbjornsen over the last two weeks, young players are showing they are capable of winning on the PGA Tour and Brown has the obvious form and pedigree.

        Ben James (80-1, Caesars Sportsbook)

        Like Koivun and Thorbjornsen, Ben James was recently promoted to the PGA Tour via PGA Tour U. 

        Since this promotion, James has made seven of eight cuts, including a T-4 at the Corales Puntacana Championship last month. 

        James just wrapped a career at the University of Virginia, where he became just the fifth player ever to be a first-team All-American in all four years of his career.
